title: Classic Brain Teasers & Puzzles
relevance: In quant and tech interviews the final answer matters less than narrating invariants, base-case checks, and logical deductions out loud.

phases.goal: Establish the puzzle-solver toolkit: invariants, working backwards, extremes, symmetry, and information framing.

must_hit.point: Look for invariants and parity—quantities that never change, such as odd/even counts, total mass, or total time.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate names invariants/parity as a first-pass tool before proposing a solution.

must_hit.point: Work backwards from the desired end state by reversing operations.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate describes starting from the goal and reversing steps rather than only forward search.

must_hit.point: A balance scale has 3 states (left down, right down, balanced), so k weighings can distinguish up to 3^k possibilities.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate states the three outcomes per weighing and the 3^k information bound.

must_hit.point: In weighing/testing puzzles, reframe around how much information each test provides (bits or base-3 states), not just the items themselves.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate talks about encoding outcomes or information capacity of each test.

probes: What general techniques do you reach for before diving into a specific brain teaser?
Why is a balance scale more powerful than a simple yes/no test per weighing?

hints.1: Think about what stays the same across moves, and what each experiment tells you.
hints.2: Name tools: invariants/parity, work backwards, edge cases, symmetry, and information per test.
hints.3: A balance has three outcomes per weighing, so k weighings distinguish up to 3^k cases; also check extremes like 1, 0, or infinity items.

phases.goal: Show how classic weighing, transport, timing, and encoding puzzles actually resolve.

must_hit.point: With 9 balls and one heavier, split into groups of 3; two weighings suffice and are optimal because 3^2 = 9.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate describes 3-vs-3 then 1-vs-1 on the suspect trio, and cites the 3^k bound.

must_hit.point: Bridge crossing with times 1, 2, 5, and 10: send the two slowest together so slow times overlap, shuttle with the two fastest; minimum is 17 minutes.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate gives the 1+2 cross, 1 back, 5+10 cross, 2 back, 1+2 cross sequence totaling 17.

must_hit.point: Irregular 60-minute ropes: lighting both ends finishes a rope in 30 minutes; then lighting the second rope’s other end yields 15 more minutes for 45 total.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate explains both-ends = 30 regardless of irregularity, then dual-light the remainder for 15.

must_hit.point: 100 prisoners / 100 boxes: each follows the cycle starting at their own box number; they succeed iff no cycle is longer than 50 (~31% chance).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate describes open box k → follow slip to next box, and states the no-cycle-over-50 win condition.

probes: How do you find the heavy ball among 9 with a balance in the minimum weighings?
Walk through the minimum-time bridge strategy for people taking 1, 2, 5, and 10 minutes.
How do you measure 45 minutes with two irregular 60-minute ropes?

hints.1: For weighing, think in equal-sized groups; for the bridge, avoid sending the fastest back every time.
hints.2: 9 balls: 3-vs-3 then refine the heavy trio. Bridge: overlap 5 and 10, use 1 and 2 as shuttle. Ropes: both ends first.
hints.3: Answer shapes: 2 weighings for 9 balls; bridge total 17; ropes give 30 then 15 for 45; prisoners follow cycles capped at length 50.

phases.goal: Contrast naive strategies with invariant- or encoding-based strategies the file highlights.

must_hit.point: Bridge: the common strategy of always sending the fastest person back is worse than overlapping the two slowest crossings and using both fast people to ferry the light.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate contrasts always-return-with-1 against the 5+10 together / 2 returns plan.

must_hit.point: With 2 eggs and 100 floors you cannot binary-search; space first-egg drops so remaining linear search keeps worst-case drops constant—d(d+1)/2 ≥ 100 gives d = 14.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate rejects pure binary search and derives triangular spacing ending at 14.

must_hit.point: Identical ants that bounce and reverse are macroscopically the same as passing through; max time is one ant walking the full rod length.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate says bounce ≈ ghost-through, so max is 100 seconds on a 100 cm rod at 1 cm/s.

must_hit.point: For fair change with 2 cuts on a 7-segment bar, binary pieces 1, 2, and 4 beat arbitrary splits because they can form every total from 1 to 7.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate chooses cuts yielding 1, 2, 4 and explains make-change in binary.

probes: Why is always sending the fastest person back on the bridge suboptimal?
With only two eggs, why isn’t binary search the right worst-case plan?
How does the bounce-vs-pass-through view change the ant-on-a-rod problem?

hints.1: Compare the obvious greedy plan to one that uses an invariant or equalizes worst case.
hints.2: Bridge: overlap slow crossings. Eggs: keep remaining drops equal after a break. Ants: treat collisions as identity-preserving pass-through.
hints.3: Bridge optimum 17; eggs need d=14 because 13·14/2=91 < 100 and 14·15/2=105 ≥ 100; ants max 100 seconds; gold pieces 1, 2, 4.

phases.goal: Apply toolkit ideas to information encoding, impossibility proofs, surface paths, and common-knowledge puzzles.

must_hit.point: Poisoned bottle among 1000 with 10 prisoners in 24 hours: map bottles to binary; each prisoner is a bit and drinks where that bit is 1; deaths encode the bottle (2^10 = 1024 ≥ 1000).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate assigns bit positions to prisoners and reads the death pattern as the bottle number.

must_hit.point: Mutilated 8×8 board (two opposite corners removed, 62 squares): every domino covers one black and one white, but opposite corners are the same color, so black/white counts differ and tiling is impossible.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate cites the coloring invariant and unequal color counts after removing same-color corners.

must_hit.point: Shortest surface path on a cube of edge s between opposite corners: unfold two faces into a 2s×s rectangle; straight-line length is s√5.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate unfolds to 2s×s and computes √((2s)^2+s^2)=s√5, rejecting through-cube s√3.

must_hit.point: Blue-eyed islanders: the visitor’s “at least one has blue eyes” creates common knowledge; if exactly n have blue eyes, all n leave on night n.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate inducts from n=1 leaving night 1 up to all n leaving on night n.

probes: How do 10 taste testers identify 1 poisoned bottle among 1000 in one 24-hour wait?
Can a chessboard with two opposite corners removed be tiled with dominoes—and why?
What is the shortest surface path for an ant between opposite corners of a cube?

hints.1: Think encoding for testers, invariants for tiling, and unfolding for surface distance.
hints.2: Bottles ↔ binary bits on prisoners; dominoes preserve black−white=0; cube path = straight line on an unfolding.
hints.3: 2^10=1024 covers 1000 bottles; same-color corners leave unequal colors so no tiling; unfold to 2s×s giving s√5; n blue-eyed leave on night n.

tradeoffs.topic: Always send fastest back vs overlap two slowest (bridge)
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Sending person 1 back every time fails to overlap the expensive 5 and 10 crossings; instead 1 and 2 shuttle while 5 and 10 cross together, totaling 17 minutes.

tradeoffs.topic: Measure rope time by length vs light both ends
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Irregular burn rates make length meaningless; lighting both ends consumes the whole rope in 30 minutes regardless, which unlocks the 45-minute construction.

tradeoffs.topic: Binary search vs constant worst-case drops (2 eggs, 100 floors)
tradeoffs.strong_answer: After the first egg breaks you must go linearly, so space first-egg drops at d, d+(d-1), … with d(d+1)/2 ≥ 100; minimum guaranteed drops is 14.

tradeoffs.topic: Model ant collisions as bounces vs as pass-through
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Identical ants reversing on collision are equivalent to ghosts passing through; the max time is walking the full 100 cm rod at 1 cm/s = 100 seconds.

tradeoffs.topic: Arbitrary gold cuts vs binary 1-2-4 pieces
tradeoffs.strong_answer: With exactly 2 cuts on 7 segments, pieces of 1, 2, and 4 can form every daily payment from 1 to 7 via make-change.

tradeoffs.topic: Think about items vs think about information per test
tradeoffs.strong_answer: A balance’s 3 outcomes mean k weighings separate up to 3^k cases; binary live/die testers map items to bit positions (e.g., 10 prisoners → 1024 bottles).

gotchas.trap: On the bridge, always sending the fastest person back with the flashlight.
gotchas.correction: That wastes slow crossings; send 5 and 10 together and use 1 and 2 to ferry so the minimum is 17 minutes.

gotchas.trap: Trying to measure time by rope length when burn rates are irregular.
gotchas.correction: Length is useless; only whole-rope facts hold—both ends finish in 30 minutes, enabling the 45-minute method.

gotchas.trap: Trying to derive the exact ~31% survival probability for the 100 prisoners in your head.
gotchas.correction: Explain cycle-following clearly and state success hinges on no cycle longer than 50; do not compute the sum on the spot.

gotchas.trap: Tracking every bounce on the ant-on-a-rod problem.
gotchas.correction: The bounce is a distraction; identical elastic reversals equal pass-through, so max time is end-to-end travel (100 seconds).

gotchas.trap: Dismissing the blue-eyes announcement as redundant because everyone already sees blue eyes.
gotchas.correction: The announcement creates common knowledge, which starts the induction so all n leave on night n.

gotchas.trap: Using s√3 as the ant’s path on the cube surface.
gotchas.correction: s√3 is the straight path through the interior; on the surface, unfold to a 2s×s rectangle and take s√5.

gotchas.trap: Assuming two eggs allow binary search of 100 floors.
gotchas.correction: One break forces linear search with the last egg; equalize worst case with triangular spacing, giving 14 drops.

gotchas.trap: Claiming the mutilated chessboard can be tiled if rotations are allowed.
gotchas.correction: Coloring is the invariant: opposite corners are the same color, leaving unequal black and white counts, so no domino tiling exists.
